must_remember: Real expansion of a liquid is the sum of apparent expansion and volume expansion of the container: $\gamma_r = \gamma_a + 3\alpha_g$.
Water exhibits anomalous expansion between $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $4^\circ\text{C}$, achieving maximum density of $1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ at $4^\circ\text{C}$.
When a liquid-filled vessel is heated, the liquid level initially drops because the solid vessel expands first before the heat reaches the liquid.
Density varies with temperature according to the relation $\rho_t \approx \rho_0 (1 - \gamma\Delta t)$ for small temperature variations.
The volume expansion coefficient of an isotropic solid container is related to its linear expansion coefficient by $\gamma_g = 3\alpha_g$.

glossary.meaning: The actual true expansion of a liquid per unit original volume per degree rise in temperature.
The observed expansion of a liquid contained in a vessel, uncorrected for the container's own expansion.
The unusual behavior of water where it contracts upon heating from $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $4^\circ\text{C}$ instead of expanding.
The fractional change in length per degree rise in temperature for a solid material.
